questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3d electron of the $Mn^{2+}$ ion (Z = 25), whose configuration is $[Ar]3d^5$. Multiply the value by 10 and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The four other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.40$. All eighteen electrons in the 1s to 3p shells screen $1.00$ each for $18.00$. Total screening is $19.40$, so $Z_{eff} = 25 - 19.40 = 5.60$ and $10 \times 5.60 = 56$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For a $Cu^{2+}$ ion (Z = 29, configuration $[Ar]3d^9$), find the effective nuclear charge on one 3d electron, multiply it by 10, and report the integer result.
questions.explanation: The eight other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.80$. The eighteen electrons in the 1s to 3p shells screen $1.00$ each for $18.00$. Total screening is $20.80$, so $Z_{eff} = 29 - 20.80 = 8.20$ and $10 \times 8.20 = 82$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What is the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3d electron of the $Cr^{3+}$ ion (Z = 24), whose configuration is $[Ar]3d^3$, after accounting for all shielding?
questions.explanation: The two other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $0.70$. The eighteen inner electrons screen $1.00$ each for $18.00$. Total screening is $18.70$, so $Z_{eff} = 24 - 18.70 = 5.30$. Ignoring the 3d partners gives 4.00, reporting total screening gives 18.70, and screening the inner shells at 0.85 gives 6.35.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What percentage of the nuclear charge of an $Fe^{2+}$ ion (Z = 26, configuration $[Ar]3d^6$) is screened from one 3d electron, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The five other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.75$. The eighteen inner electrons screen $18.00$ in total. Total screening is $19.75$, and $19.75/26 = 0.7596$, which is 76 percent after rounding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge experienced by one 3d electron of a neutral titanium atom (Z = 22), whose configuration is $[Ar]3d^2 4s^2$.
questions.explanation: The other 3d electron screens $0.35$. The eighteen electrons in the 1s to 3p shells screen $1.00$ each for $18.00$, and the 4s electrons screen nothing for a 3d electron in this scheme. Total screening is $18.35$, so $Z_{eff} = 22 - 18.35 = 3.65$. Ignoring the 3d partner gives 4.00, reporting total screening gives 18.35, and screening the inner shells at 0.85 gives 6.35.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge of a 1s electron in a beryllium ion with only two electrons, $Be^{2+}$ (Z = 4). Multiply the value by 10 and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The other 1s electron is the only partner, and it screens $0.30$. So $Z_{eff} = 4 - 0.30 = 3.70$, and $10 \times 3.70 = 37$. Using a 0.35 partner screening instead of 0.30 would be a common slip for 1s electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What percentage of the nuclear charge of a $Li^{+}$ ion (Z = 3) is screened from its only 1s partner electron, rounded to the nearest whole percent, given that the ion carries two electrons?
questions.explanation: The single 1s partner screens $0.30$. The screened fraction is $0.30/3 = 0.10$, or 10 percent, which is the whole-number result.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In a Moseley-type relation the square root of the X-ray frequency equals 6 times (Z minus 2), in chosen units. A line has a square-root frequency of 96 units. What is the atomic number of the emitting element?
questions.explanation: Dividing the square-root frequency by 6 gives $Z - 2 = 96/6 = 16$. Adding 2 gives $Z = 18$, which corresponds to argon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Pauling electronegativities are 0.93 for Na, 1.31 for Mg and 1.61 for Al. What is the mean electronegativity of these three elements, to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: The sum is $0.93 + 1.31 + 1.61 = 3.85$. Dividing by 3 gives $3.85/3 = 1.283$, which rounds to 1.28. Reporting the Mg value alone gives 1.31, reporting the Al value gives 1.61, and averaging only Na and Al gives 1.27.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3p electron of the $Ca^{2+}$ ion (Z = 20), which carries eighteen electrons in its ground state, $[Ar]$.
questions.explanation: The seven other 3s/3p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.45$. The eight 2s/2p electrons screen $0.85$ each for $6.80$, and the 1s pair screens $2.00$. Total screening is $11.25$, so $Z_{eff} = 20 - 11.25 = 8.75$. Copying the $K^{+}$ value gives 7.75, ignoring the 2s/2p shell gives 15.55, and reporting total screening gives 11.25.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What percentage of the nuclear charge of a $Cu^{2+}$ ion (Z = 29) is screened from one 3d electron by all the other electrons, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: Total screening is $2.80 + 18.00 = 20.80$, from the eight partner 3d electrons ($0.35$ each) and the eighteen inner electrons ($1.00$ each). The screened fraction is $20.80/29 = 0.7172$, which rounds to 72 percent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What is the difference between the 3d effective nuclear charges of $Fe^{3+}$ (Z = 26, $[Ar]3d^5$) and $Fe^{2+}$ (Z = 26, $[Ar]3d^6$), to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: For $Fe^{2+}$ the five partner 3d electrons give $5 \times 0.35 = 1.75$, so $Z_{eff} = 26 - 19.75 = 6.25$. For $Fe^{3+}$ the four partners give $1.40$, so $Z_{eff} = 26 - 19.40 = 6.60$. The difference is $6.60 - 6.25 = 0.35$. Doubling the difference gives 0.70, quoting the group term gives 1.75, and quoting the $Fe^{3+}$ value gives 6.60.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Find the effective nuclear charge felt by one 1s electron of a neutral helium atom (Z = 2), multiply it by 10, and give the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The partner 1s electron screens $0.30$, so $Z_{eff} = 2 - 0.30 = 1.70$. Multiplying by 10 gives $17$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the 3d effective nuclear charge of a $Ti^{3+}$ ion (Z = 22, $[Ar]3d^1$), multiply it by 10, and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The single 3d electron has no 3d partners, so only the eighteen inner electrons screen, giving $18.00$. Then $Z_{eff} = 22 - 18.00 = 4.00$, and $10 \times 4.00 = 40$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3d electron of a $V^{2+}$ ion (Z = 23, $[Ar]3d^3$). Multiply the value by 10 and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The two other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $0.70$. The eighteen inner electrons screen $18.00$ in total. Total screening is $18.70$, so $Z_{eff} = 23 - 18.70 = 4.30$ and $10 \times 4.30 = 43$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the 3d effective nuclear charges of these ions. I. The 3d electrons of $Mn^{2+}$ feel a lower value than those of $Fe^{2+}$. II. The 3d electrons of $Cu^{2+}$ feel a higher value than those of $Fe^{2+}$. III. The 3d electrons of $Cr^{3+}$ feel a higher value than those of $Mn^{2+}$. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: $Mn^{2+}$ gives $Z_{eff} = 5.60$ and $Fe^{2+}$ gives 6.25, so I is true. $Cu^{2+}$ gives 8.20, so II is true. $Cr^{3+}$ gives 5.30, which is lower than $Mn^{2+}$ at 5.60, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider these aqueous stability statements about transition metal ions. I. $Mn^{2+}$ is more stable than $Mn^{3+}$. II. $Cr^{3+}$ is more stable than $Cr^{2+}$. III. $Cr^{2+}$ is more stable than $Cr^{3+}$. IV. $Co^{2+}$ is more stable than $Co^{3+}$. How many of these four statements are correct?
questions.explanation: $Mn^{2+}$ is the most stable manganese ion in water, so I is true. $Cr^{2+}$ is a strong reducing agent that is readily oxidised to $Cr^{3+}$, so II is true and III is false. $Co^{3+}$ is a strong oxidant that oxidises water, so IV is true. Three statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the metallic character of Group 14 elements. I. Sn is more metallic than C. II. Pb has a lower first ionisation enthalpy than Sn. III. Ge is a metalloid. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Sn is metallic whereas C is a non-metal, so I is true. Pb (715 kJ/mol) has a higher IE1 than Sn (709 kJ/mol), so II is false. Ge is classified as a metalloid, so III is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the sizes of Group 1 ions. I. $K^{+}$ is larger than $Na^{+}$. II. $Rb^{+}$ is smaller than $K^{+}$. III. $Li^{+}$ is smaller than $Na^{+}$. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: $K^{+}$ (138 pm) is larger than $Na^{+}$ (102 pm), so I is true. $Rb^{+}$ (152 pm) is larger than $K^{+}$, so II is false. $Li^{+}$ (76 pm) is smaller than $Na^{+}$, so III is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the 3d effective nuclear charges of Mn2+ (Z = 25), Fe2+ (Z = 26), Fe3+ (Z = 26), Cr3+ (Z = 24) and Cu2+ (Z = 29). How many of these ions have a 3d effective nuclear charge greater than 6.0?
questions.explanation: The values are Mn2+ 5.60, Fe2+ 6.25, Fe3+ 6.60, Cr3+ 5.30 and Cu2+ 8.20. Only Fe2+, Fe3+ and Cu2+ exceed 6.0, so the count is 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the successive ionisation enthalpies of iron, IE1 = 762, IE2 = 1562 and IE3 = 2957 kJ/mol. I. IE2 is greater than IE1. II. The ratio IE3/IE2 exceeds 1.8. III. IE2 is smaller than IE1. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: IE2 (1562) is greater than IE1 (762), so I is true. The ratio $2957/1562 = 1.89$ exceeds 1.8, so II is true. IE2 cannot be smaller than IE1 because removing a second electron from a positive ion always costs more, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the Pauling electronegativities of Fe (1.83), Cu (1.90) and Zn (1.65). I. Cu is more electronegative than Fe. II. Zn is less electronegative than Fe. III. Cu is less electronegative than Zn. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Cu (1.90) is more electronegative than Fe (1.83), so I is true. Zn (1.65) is less electronegative than Fe (1.83), so II is true. Cu (1.90) is higher than Zn (1.65), so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the 3d effective nuclear charge of $Mn^{2+}$ and of $Fe^{2+}$. What percentage of the nuclear charge of $Mn^{2+}$ (Z = 25) is screened from its 3d electron, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The total screening for a 3d electron of $Mn^{2+}$ is $1.40 + 18.00 = 19.40$. The screened fraction is $19.40/25 = 0.776$, which is 77.6 percent and rounds to 78.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge experienced by one 4s electron of a neutral titanium atom (Z = 22, $[Ar]3d^2 4s^2$), using the usual screening conventions.
questions.explanation: The partner 4s electron screens $0.35$. The ten 3s, 3p and 3d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $8.50$, and the ten 1s, 2s and 2p electrons screen $1.00$ each for $10.00$. Total screening is $18.85$, so $Z_{eff} = 22 - 18.85 = 3.15$. Copying the calcium value gives 2.85, quoting the 3d value gives 3.65, and copying the zinc value gives 4.35.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the 4s effective nuclear charges of Ca (2.85), Sc (3.00), Ti (3.15), Cr (2.95), Cu (3.70) and Zn (4.35). How many of these have a 4s effective nuclear charge greater than 3.00?
questions.explanation: Ti (3.15), Cu (3.70) and Zn (4.35) exceed 3.00. Ca (2.85), Sc (3.00, which is equal and not greater) and Cr (2.95) do not, so the count is 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the first ionisation enthalpies of some s-block and p-block elements. I. Mg has a higher IE1 than Al. II. Ca has a lower IE1 than Mg. III. Ba has a higher IE1 than Sr. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Mg (738) is higher than Al (578), so I is true. Ca (590) is lower than Mg (738), so II is true. Ba (503) is lower than Sr (549), so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the 3p effective nuclear charges of $K^{+}$ (Z = 19), $Ca^{2+}$ (Z = 20), $Cl^{-}$ (Z = 17) and $S^{2-}$ (Z = 16), each treated with usual screening conventions. How many of these four species have a 3p effective nuclear charge above 7.0?
questions.explanation: The values are $K^{+}$ 7.75, $Ca^{2+}$ 8.75, $Cl^{-}$ 5.75 and $S^{2-}$ 4.75. Only $K^{+}$ and $Ca^{2+}$ exceed 7.0, so the count is 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compute the ratio of the 3d effective nuclear charge of $Fe^{2+}$ to that of $Mn^{2+}$, using the usual screening conventions, to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: $Fe^{2+}$ gives $Z_{eff} = 6.25$ and $Mn^{2+}$ gives $Z_{eff} = 5.60$. The ratio is $6.25/5.60 = 1.116$, which rounds to 1.12. Inverting the ratio gives 0.90, taking the difference gives 0.65, and assuming equal values gives 1.00.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The 3d effective nuclear charge of $Mn^{2+}$ is 5.60 and that of $Fe^{2+}$ is 6.25. What is the percentage increase going from the Mn2+ value to the Fe2+ value, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The increase is $6.25 - 5.60 = 0.65$. Relative to the Mn2+ value, this is $0.65/5.60 = 0.116$, or 11.6 percent, which rounds to 12.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare copper ions and their sizes and stabilities. I. The 3d electrons of $Cu^{2+}$ feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of $Cu^{+}$. II. $Cu^{+}$ is more stable than $Cu^{2+}$ in aqueous solution. III. $Cu^{2+}$ is smaller than $Cu^{+}$. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: $Cu^{2+}$ gives $Z_{eff} = 8.20$, while $Cu^{+}$ gives 7.85, so I is true. In water $Cu^{2+}$ is the more stable ion, so II is false. The radii are about 73 pm for $Cu^{2+}$ and 77 pm for $Cu^{+}$, so III is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the 3p effective nuclear charges of these species. I. The 3p electrons of $Ca^{2+}$ feel a higher value than those of $K^{+}$. II. The 3p electrons of Ar feel a lower value than those of $Ca^{2+}$. III. The 3p electrons of $K^{+}$ feel a lower value than those of Ar. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: $Ca^{2+}$ gives 8.75 and $K^{+}$ gives 7.75, so I is true. Ar gives 6.75, which is lower than $Ca^{2+}$ at 8.75, so II is true. $K^{+}$ gives 7.75, which is higher than Ar at 6.75, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the 3d effective nuclear charge of a $Cu^{+}$ ion (Z = 29, $[Ar]3d^{10}$). What percentage of the nuclear charge is screened from one 3d electron, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The nine partner 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $3.15$, and the eighteen inner electrons screen $18.00$. Total screening is $21.15$, and $21.15/29 = 0.729$, which rounds to 73 percent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the acid-base character of the Group 13 oxides. I. $Al_2O_3$ is amphoteric. II. $B_2O_3$ is amphoteric. III. $Al_2O_3$ is more basic than $B_2O_3$. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: $Al_2O_3$ reacts with both acids and strong bases, so I is true. $B_2O_3$ is acidic rather than amphoteric, so II is false. $Al_2O_3$ is more basic than $B_2O_3$, which is strongly acidic, so III is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Iron has successive ionisation enthalpies of 762 kJ/mol (IE1) and 1562 kJ/mol (IE2). Divide IE2 by IE1 and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The ratio is $1562/762 = 2.05$, which rounds to 2. The second electron is removed at roughly twice the energy of the first.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the 3d effective nuclear charge felt by one electron of a $Ni^{2+}$ ion (Z = 28, $[Ar]3d^8$), using the usual screening conventions.
questions.explanation: The seven other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.45$. The eighteen inner electrons screen $18.00$. Total screening is $20.45$, so $Z_{eff} = 28 - 20.45 = 7.55$. Quoting the Ni neutral 4s value gives 4.05, copying the Cu2+ value gives 8.20, and reporting the total screening gives 20.45.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the 3d effective nuclear charges of selected ions, estimated with standard screening constants. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: A) The 3d electrons of $Fe^{2+}$ feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of $Mn^{2+}$, about $6.25$ against $5.60$.
B) The 3d electrons of $Fe^{3+}$ feel a lower effective nuclear charge than those of $Cu^{2+}$, about $6.60$ against $8.20$.
C) The 3d electrons of $Cr^{3+}$ feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of $Ti^{3+}$, about $5.30$ against $4.00$.
D) The 3d electrons of $Cu^{+}$ feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of $Cu^{2+}$, about $7.85$ against $8.20$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Using electronegativities and ionisation enthalpies of d-block and neighbouring elements, which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply, using standard textbook values.
options: A) Cu (Pauling 1.90) is more electronegative than Fe (Pauling 1.83).
B) The first ionisation enthalpy of Zn (906 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Cu (745 kJ/mol).
C) The first ionisation enthalpy of Ca (590 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Sc (633 kJ/mol).
D) The first ionisation enthalpy of Mn (717 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Fe (762 kJ/mol).
questions.explanation: Cu $(1.90)$ is above Fe $(1.83)$, so A is correct. Zn $(906)$ is above Cu $(745)$, so B is correct. Ca $(590)$ is below Sc $(633)$ because the rising nuclear charge outweighs the poor shielding of the added 3d electron, so C is false. Mn $(717)$ is below Fe $(762)$, so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the stability of oxidation states in Group 14 and Group 15 elements, which reflect the inert pair effect and related trends. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: A) $Pb^{2+}$ is more stable than $Pb^{4+}$ in aqueous solution.
B) $Sn^{4+}$ is a stronger reducing agent than $Sn^{2+}$.
D) The electron gain enthalpy of N is more negative than that of O.
questions.explanation: The inert pair effect makes $Pb^{2+}$ more stable than $Pb^{4+}$, so A is correct. $Sn^{2+}$ is the reducing form, so B is false. $Bi^{5+}$ is a strong oxidant, so $Bi^{3+}$ is the stable ion, making C correct. Nitrogen's electron gain enthalpy is near zero or positive, far less negative than oxygen's (-141), so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the 3d effective nuclear charge of $Cu^{2+}$ (Z = 29) and of $Ti^{3+}$ (Z = 22), using the usual screening conventions. Divide the first value by the second and round the ratio to the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3d electron of a $Co^{2+}$ ion (Z = 27, $[Ar]3d^7$), using the usual screening conventions. Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: The six other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.10$. The eighteen inner electrons screen $18.00$. Total screening is $20.10$, so $Z_{eff} = 27 - 20.10 = 6.90$. Quoting the $Fe^{2+}$ value gives 6.25, quoting the $Ni^{2+}$ value gives 7.55, and reporting total screening gives 20.10.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the 4s and 3d effective nuclear charges of selected atoms and ions. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply, using usual screening conventions.
options: A) The 4s electrons of Ti (about $3.15$) feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of Ca (about $2.85$).
B) The 3d electrons of Zn (about $8.85$) feel a lower effective nuclear charge than those of Ti (about $3.65$).
C) The 3d electrons of $Fe^{2+}$ (about $6.25$) feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of $Co^{2+}$ (about $6.90$).
D) The 3d electrons of Ti (about $3.65$) feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of Sc (about $3.00$).
questions.explanation: Ti 4s gives $22 - 18.85 = 3.15$, above Ca 4s at $20 - 17.15 = 2.85$, so A is correct. Zn 3d gives $30 - 21.15 = 8.85$, which is higher, not lower, than Ti 3d at $22 - 18.35 = 3.65$, so B is false. $Fe^{2+}$ at 6.25 is lower than $Co^{2+}$ at 6.90, so C is false. Ti 3d at 3.65 exceeds Sc 3d at $21 - 18.00 = 3.00$, so D is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the Pauling electronegativities and first ionisation enthalpies of Group 13 and Group 14 elements. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: A) The Pauling electronegativity of Ga (1.81) exceeds that of Al (1.61).
B) The first ionisation enthalpy of Ga (579 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Al (578 kJ/mol).
C) The first ionisation enthalpy of Ge (762 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Si (787 kJ/mol).
D) The first ionisation enthalpy of Ge (762 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Sn (708 kJ/mol).
questions.explanation: Ga $(1.81)$ is above Al $(1.61)$, so A is correct. Ga's IE1 of $579$ kJ/mol is just above Al's $578$ kJ/mol because the $3d^{10}$ electrons shield poorly, so B is correct. Ge $(762)$ is below Si $(787)$, so C is false. Ge $(762)$ is above Sn $(708)$, so D is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Count how many of the following statements are correct. (i) The 3d effective nuclear charge of $Fe^{2+}$ exceeds that of $Mn^{2+}$. (ii) The 3d effective nuclear charge of $Co^{2+}$ exceeds that of $Fe^{2+}$. (iii) The 3d effective nuclear charge of $Ti^{3+}$ exceeds that of $Cr^{3+}$. (iv) The 3d effective nuclear charge of $Cu^{2+}$ exceeds that of $Zn^{2+}$.
questions.explanation: $Fe^{2+}$ (6.25) exceeds $Mn^{2+}$ (5.60), so (i) is correct. $Co^{2+}$ (6.90) exceeds $Fe^{2+}$ (6.25), so (ii) is correct. $Ti^{3+}$ (4.00) is below $Cr^{3+}$ (5.30), so (iii) is false. $Zn^{2+}$ (8.85) exceeds $Cu^{2+}$ (8.20), so (iv) is false. Two statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge experienced by the 4s electron of a neutral vanadium atom (Z = 23, $[Ar]3d^3 4s^2$), using the usual screening conventions. Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: The partner 4s electron screens $0.35$. The eleven 3s, 3p and 3d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $9.35$, and the ten 1s, 2s and 2p electrons screen $1.00$ each for $10.00$. Total screening is $19.70$, so $Z_{eff} = 23 - 19.70 = 3.30$. Copying the titanium value gives 3.15, ignoring the 3d electrons gives 5.85, and reporting total screening gives 19.70.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3p electron of the $Sc^{3+}$ ion (Z = 21), which carries eighteen electrons in its ground state, $[Ar]$, using the usual screening conventions.
questions.explanation: The seven partner 3s/3p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.45$. The eight 2s/2p electrons screen $0.85$ each for $6.80$, and the 1s pair screens $2.00$. Total screening is $11.25$, so $Z_{eff} = 21 - 11.25 = 9.75$. Copying the argon value gives 6.75, ignoring the 1s screening gives 11.75, and reporting total screening gives 11.25.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compute the ratio of the 3p effective nuclear charge of $Sc^{3+}$ to that of neutral argon, using usual screening conventions. Round the ratio to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The $Sc^{3+}$ 3p value is $21 - 11.25 = 9.75$ and the argon 3p value is $18 - 11.25 = 6.75$. The ratio $9.75/6.75 = 1.44$ rounds to 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3d electron of a neutral chromium atom (Z = 24, $[Ar]3d^5 4s^1$), using the usual screening conventions. Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: The four other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.40$. The eighteen inner electrons screen $1.00$ each for $18.00$. Total screening is $19.40$, so $Z_{eff} = 24 - 19.40 = 4.60$. Quoting the $Mn^{2+}$ value gives 5.60, quoting the $Fe^{2+}$ value gives 6.25, and reporting total screening gives 19.40.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Divide the 3d effective nuclear charge of $Fe^{3+}$ (Z = 26, $[Ar]3d^5$) by that of $Fe^{2+}$ (Z = 26, $[Ar]3d^6$), using the usual screening conventions, and round the ratio to the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Using Pauling electronegativities of 1.81 for Ga and 3.16 for Cl, estimate the percentage ionic character of the GaCl bond, rounded to the nearest whole percent.
questions.explanation: The difference is $\Delta\chi = 3.16 - 1.81 = 1.35$, so $\Delta\chi^2/4 = 1.8225/4 = 0.456$. The ionic character is $100(1 - e^{-0.456}) = 100(1 - 0.634) = 36.6$, which rounds to 37. Quoting the covalent fraction gives 63, skipping the square gives 19, and reporting the raw difference as a percentage gives 1.35.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 4p electron of a neutral bromine atom (Z = 35), whose configuration is $[Ar]3d^{10}4s^2 4p^5$.
questions.explanation: The six other 4s/4p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.10$. The eighteen electrons in the 3s, 3p and 3d shells screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$, and the ten 1s, 2s and 2p electrons screen $1.00$ each for $10.00$. Total screening is $27.40$, so $Z_{eff} = 35 - 27.40 = 7.60$. Copying the selenium value gives 6.95, reporting total screening gives 27.40, and treating the 3d electrons at 1.00 gives 6.10.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What percentage of the nuclear charge of a selenium atom (Z = 34, $[Ar]3d^{10}4s^2 4p^4$) is screened from one 4p electron by the other electrons, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The five other 4s/4p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.75$. The eighteen 3s/3p/3d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$, and the ten inner electrons screen $10.00$. Total screening is $27.05$, and $27.05/34 = 0.7956$, which rounds to 80 percent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Find the effective nuclear charge felt by one 4p electron of an arsenic atom (Z = 33, $[Ar]3d^{10}4s^2 4p^3$), multiply it by 10, and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The four other 4s/4p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.40$. The eighteen 3s/3p/3d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$, and the ten inner electrons screen $10.00$. Total screening is $26.70$, so $Z_{eff} = 33 - 26.70 = 6.30$ and $10 \times 6.30 = 63$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What percentage of the nuclear charge of a bromide ion ($Br^{-}$, Z = 35, 36 electrons) is screened from one 4p electron, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The seven other 4s/4p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.45$. The eighteen 3s/3p/3d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$, and the ten inner electrons screen $10.00$. Total screening is $27.75$, and $27.75/35 = 0.7929$, which rounds to 79 percent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Two bonded atoms have Pauling electronegativities of 2.20 for hydrogen and 2.96 for bromine. Estimate the percentage ionic character of the H-Br bond, rounded to the nearest whole percent.
questions.explanation: The difference is $\Delta\chi = 2.96 - 2.20 = 0.76$, so $\Delta\chi^2/4 = 0.5776/4 = 0.144$. The ionic character is $100(1 - e^{-0.144}) = 100(1 - 0.866) = 13.4$, which rounds to 13.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Hypothetical atoms P and Q have single-bond energies of 150 kJ/mol (P-P), 250 kJ/mol (Q-Q) and 390 kJ/mol (P-Q). Estimate the Pauling electronegativity difference between P and Q to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The excess bond energy is $\Delta = 390 - \sqrt{150 \times 250} = 390 - 193.65 = 196.35$ kJ/mol. Pauling's relation $\Delta = 96.5(\chi_P - \chi_Q)^2$ gives $(\chi_P - \chi_Q)^2 = 2.03$, so the difference is $\sqrt{2.03} = 1.43$. Reporting the squared value gives 2.03, inverting the answer gives 0.70, and a rounded wrong bond energy gives 1.20.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In a Moseley-type relation the square root of the X-ray frequency equals 7 times (Z minus 1), in chosen units. A line has a square-root frequency of 245 units. What is the atomic number of the emitting element?
questions.explanation: Dividing the square-root frequency by 7 gives $Z - 1 = 245/7 = 35$. Adding 1 gives $Z = 36$, which corresponds to krypton.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Find the mean first ionisation enthalpy, in kJ/mol to the nearest whole number, of oxygen (1314), sulphur (1000) and selenium (941) taken together.
questions.explanation: The sum is $1314 + 1000 + 941 = 3255$ kJ/mol. Dividing by 3 gives $3255/3 = 1085$ kJ/mol. Reporting only the sulphur value gives 1000, averaging just O and S gives 1157, and reporting Se alone gives 941.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the percentage ionic character of the H-Cl bond using Pauling electronegativities of 2.20 for H and 3.16 for Cl, rounded to the nearest whole percent.
questions.explanation: The difference is $\Delta\chi = 3.16 - 2.20 = 0.96$, so $\Delta\chi^2/4 = 0.9216/4 = 0.230$. The ionic character is $100(1 - e^{-0.230}) = 100(1 - 0.795) = 20.5$, which rounds to 21.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the effective nuclear charges felt by the 4p electrons of bromine (Z = 35) and selenium (Z = 34). What is the ratio of the bromine value to the selenium value, to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: Bromine 4p gives $Z_{eff} = 7.60$, and selenium 4p gives $Z_{eff} = 34 - 27.05 = 6.95$. The ratio is $7.60/6.95 = 1.094$, which rounds to 1.09. Inverting the ratio gives 0.91, taking the difference gives 0.65, and quoting the bromine value alone gives 7.60.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Find the difference between the effective nuclear charges felt by one 4p electron of bromine (Z = 35) and of arsenic (Z = 33). Multiply the difference by 10 and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: Bromine 4p gives $Z_{eff} = 7.60$ and arsenic 4p gives $Z_{eff} = 6.30$. The difference is $1.30$, and $10 \times 1.30 = 13$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3s electron of a phosphorus atom (Z = 15, $[Ne]3s^2 3p^3$). Multiply the value by 10 and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The four other 3s/3p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.40$. The eight 2s/2p electrons screen $0.85$ each for $6.80$, and the 1s pair screens $2.00$. Total screening is $10.20$, so $Z_{eff} = 15 - 10.20 = 4.80$ and $10 \times 4.80 = 48$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What percentage of the nuclear charge of a chloride ion ($Cl^{-}$, Z = 17, 18 electrons) is screened from one 3p electron, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The seven other 3s/3p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.45$. The eight 2s/2p electrons screen $0.85$ each for $6.80$, and the 1s pair screens $2.00$. Total screening is $11.25$, and $11.25/17 = 0.6618$, which rounds to 66 percent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compute the mean Pauling electronegativity of the four halogens F (3.98), Cl (3.16), Br (2.96) and I (2.66), to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The sum is $3.98 + 3.16 + 2.96 + 2.66 = 12.76$. Dividing by 4 gives $12.76/4 = 3.19$. Reporting the Cl value gives 3.16, averaging only F and I gives 3.32, and reporting the Br value gives 2.96.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Find the 3p effective nuclear charges of phosphorus (Z = 15) and silicon (Z = 14), subtract the silicon value from the phosphorus value, multiply the difference by 100, and report the integer.
questions.explanation: Phosphorus 3p gives $Z_{eff} = 15 - 10.20 = 4.80$ and silicon 3p gives $Z_{eff} = 14 - 9.85 = 4.15$. The difference is $0.65$, and $100 \times 0.65 = 65$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the first ionisation enthalpies of Group 16 elements. I. O has a higher IE1 than S. II. S has a higher IE1 than Se. III. Te has a higher IE1 than Se. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: O (1314) is higher than S (1000), so I is true. S (1000) is higher than Se (941), so II is true. Te (869) is lower than Se (941), so III is false, since IE1 falls down the group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider these comparisons among halogen species. (i) $Br^{-}$ has a larger ionic radius than $Cl^{-}$. (ii) Br has a less negative electron gain enthalpy than Cl. (iii) HF is a weaker acid than HCl in water. (iv) I is more electronegative than Br. How many of these four statements are correct?
questions.explanation: $Br^{-}$ (196 pm) is larger than $Cl^{-}$ (181 pm), so (i) is correct. Br (-325) is less negative than Cl (-349), so (ii) is correct. HF is a weak acid in water while HCl is strong, so (iii) is correct. I (2.66) is less electronegative than Br (2.96), so (iv) is false. Three statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the acidity of the hydrogen halides in aqueous solution. I. HF is the weakest acid among the hydrogen halides. II. HI is the strongest acid among the hydrogen halides. III. HCl is stronger than HBr. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: HF is a weak acid in water while the others are strong, so I is true. HI has the weakest H-X bond and is the strongest acid, so II is true. HBr is stronger than HCl because its H-Br bond is weaker, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the chemistry of beryllium oxide and its neighbours in the periodic table. I. BeO is amphoteric. II. Be(OH)$_2$ dissolves in excess NaOH. III. BeO is more basic than MgO. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: BeO reacts with both acids and strong bases, so I is true. Be(OH)$_2$ dissolves in excess NaOH to form a beryllate ion, so II is true. MgO is the more basic oxide because Be$^{2+}$ is small and highly polarising, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the percentage ionic characters estimated for NaCl (71), HF (55), HCl (21), HBr (13) and MgO (68). How many of these bonds are more than 50 percent ionic?
questions.explanation: NaCl (71), HF (55) and MgO (68) exceed 50 percent, while HCl (21) and HBr (13) do not. The count is 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the 4p effective nuclear charges of these atoms. I. The 4p electrons of Br feel a higher value than those of Se. II. The 4p electrons of As feel a lower value than those of Se. III. The 4p electrons of Se feel a higher value than those of Br. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Br 4p gives $Z_{eff} = 7.60$, above Se at 6.95, so I is true. As 4p gives 6.30, below Se at 6.95, so II is true. Se 4p at 6.95 is lower than Br 4p at 7.60, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The effective nuclear charges felt by 4p electrons are 6.95 for Se and 7.60 for Br. What is the percentage increase going from the Se value to the Br value, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The increase is $7.60 - 6.95 = 0.65$. Relative to the Se value, $0.65/6.95 = 0.0935$, or 9.35 percent, which rounds to 9.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the Pauling electronegativities of Br (2.96), I (2.66) and Te (2.10). I. Br is more electronegative than I. II. I is more electronegative than Te. III. Te is more electronegative than Se. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Br (2.96) exceeds I (2.66), so I is true. I (2.66) exceeds Te (2.10), so II is true. Se (2.55) exceeds Te (2.10), so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The first ionisation enthalpies are 1000 kJ/mol for S and 941 kJ/mol for Se. What is the percentage by which the IE1 of Se is lower than that of S, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The difference is $1000 - 941 = 59$ kJ/mol. Relative to S, the drop is $59/1000 = 0.059$, or 5.9 percent, which rounds to 6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider metallic character in the p-block. I. Bi is more metallic than Sb. II. As is more metallic than P. III. N is a metalloid. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Bi is the more metallic member of Group 15 compared with Sb, so I is true. As is more metallic than P, so II is true. N is a non-metal and not a metalloid, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider these comparisons for Group 16. (i) IE1 of S is higher than IE1 of Se. (ii) IE1 of Se is higher than IE1 of Te. (iii) Electron gain enthalpy of Se is more negative than that of S. (iv) The atomic radius of Te is larger than that of Se. How many of these statements are correct?
questions.explanation: S (1000) exceeds Se (941), so (i) is correct. Se (941) exceeds Te (869), so (ii) is correct. Se (-195) is less negative than S (-200), so (iii) is false. Te has a larger radius than Se, so (iv) is correct. Three statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the 4p effective nuclear charges of these atoms. I. Ga has a lower 4p value than Ge. II. Ge has a lower 4p value than As. III. As has a higher 4p value than Br. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Ga 4p gives 5.00 and Ge 4p gives 5.65, so I is true. Ge 4p is 5.65 and As 4p is 6.30, so II is true. As 4p (6.30) is lower than Br 4p (7.60), so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compute the ratio of the 4p effective nuclear charge of selenium to that of arsenic, multiply it by 10, and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: Selenium 4p gives $Z_{eff} = 6.95$ and arsenic 4p gives $Z_{eff} = 6.30$. The ratio is $6.95/6.30 = 1.103$, and $10 \times 1.103 = 11.03$, which rounds to 11.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the electron gain enthalpies of halogens. I. Cl has a more negative electron gain enthalpy than F. II. I has a less negative electron gain enthalpy than Br. III. Br has a more negative electron gain enthalpy than F. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Cl (-349) is more negative than F (-328), so I is true. I (-295) is less negative than Br (-325), so II is true. Br (-325) is less negative than F (-328), so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the ions $Br^{-}$, $Rb^{+}$, $Sr^{2+}$, $Se^{2-}$ and $Cl^{-}$. How many of these ions are isoelectronic with krypton (36 electrons)?
questions.explanation: $Br^{-}$ (35 + 1 = 36), $Rb^{+}$ (37 - 1 = 36), $Sr^{2+}$ (38 - 2 = 36) and $Se^{2-}$ (34 + 2 = 36) all have 36 electrons. $Cl^{-}$ has 18 electrons and does not qualify, so the count is 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the first ionisation enthalpies of Group 2 elements. I. Ba has a lower IE1 than Ca. II. Sr has a higher IE1 than Ba. III. Ca has a lower IE1 than Sr. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Ba (503) is lower than Ca (590), so I is true. Sr (549) is higher than Ba (503), so II is true. Ca (590) is higher than Sr (549), so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The first ionisation enthalpies are 941 kJ/mol for Se and 869 kJ/mol for Te. What is the percentage by which the IE1 of Te is lower than that of Se, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The difference is $941 - 869 = 72$ kJ/mol. Relative to Se, the drop is $72/941 = 0.0765$, or 7.65 percent, which rounds to 8.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compute the ratio of the first ionisation enthalpy of Ne (2081 kJ/mol) to that of Ar (1521 kJ/mol), to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The ratio is $2081/1521 = 1.368$, which rounds to 1.37. Inverting the ratio gives 0.73, dividing the difference in thousands gives 0.56, and reporting the Ne value alone gives 2081.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the first ionisation enthalpies of O (1314), S (1000), Se (941) and Te (869) kJ/mol. How many of these four elements have IE1 below 1000 kJ/mol?
questions.explanation: Only Se (941) and Te (869) are below 1000 kJ/mol. S sits exactly at 1000 and O is higher, so the count is 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3d electron of a gallium atom (Z = 31, $[Ar]3d^{10}4s^2 4p^1$), where the 4s and 4p electrons do not screen 3d electrons.
questions.explanation: The nine other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $3.15$. The eighteen electrons in the 1s to 3p shells screen $1.00$ each for $18.00$. Total screening is $21.15$, so $Z_{eff} = 31 - 21.15 = 9.85$. Copying the Ga 4p value gives 5.00, ignoring the 3s and 3p shielding gives 17.85, and reporting total screening gives 21.15.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the effective nuclear charges of selected p-block valence electrons and ions, estimated with standard screening constants. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: A) The 4p electrons of Br feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of Se, about $7.60$ against $6.95$.
B) The 4p electrons of As feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of Br, about $6.30$ against $7.60$.
C) The 4p electrons of $Br^{-}$ feel a lower effective nuclear charge than those of neutral Br, about $7.25$ against $7.60$.
D) The 4p electrons of $Se^{2-}$ feel a higher effective nuclear charge than the 5p electrons of Te, about $6.25$ against $6.95$.
questions.explanation: Br 4p gives $35 - 27.40 = 7.60$ and Se 4p gives $34 - 27.05 = 6.95$, so A is correct. As 4p gives $33 - 26.70 = 6.30$, below Br's 7.60, so B is false. $Br^{-}$ 4p gives $35 - 27.75 = 7.25$, below neutral Br at 7.60, so C is correct. $Se^{2-}$ 4p gives $34 - 27.75 = 6.25$, which is lower than Te 5p at 6.95, so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Using Pauling electronegativities (H 2.20, Se 2.55, Br 2.96, As 2.18, I 2.66, Te 2.10) and the usual percentage ionic character estimate, which statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: A) The Se-Br bond is less than 5 percent ionic.
B) The Te-I bond is more than 10 percent ionic.
C) The As-Br bond is less than 15 percent ionic.
D) The H-I bond is more than 5 percent ionic.
questions.explanation: For Se-Br, $\Delta\chi = 0.41$ gives $100(1 - e^{-0.042}) = 4.1$ percent, so A is correct. For Te-I, $\Delta\chi = 0.56$ gives $100(1 - e^{-0.078}) \approx 7.5$ percent, so B is false. For As-Br, $\Delta\chi = 0.78$ gives $100(1 - e^{-0.152}) \approx 14.1$ percent, so C is correct. For H-I, $\Delta\chi = 0.46$ gives $100(1 - e^{-0.053}) \approx 5.2$ percent, so D is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the first ionisation enthalpies and electron gain enthalpies of selected p-block elements. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply, using standard textbook values.
options: A) The first ionisation enthalpy of Te (869 kJ/mol) is lower than that of Se (941 kJ/mol).
B) The first ionisation enthalpy of As (947 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Se (941 kJ/mol).
C) The first ionisation enthalpy of Br (1140 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Se (941 kJ/mol).
D) The first ionisation enthalpy of Ga (579 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Ge (762 kJ/mol).
questions.explanation: Te $(869)$ is below Se $(941)$, so A is correct. As $(947)$ is just above Se $(941)$ because of the half-filled $4p^3$ subshell, so B is correct. Br $(1140)$ lies well above Se $(941)$ across the period, so C is correct. Ga $(579)$ is far below Ge $(762)$, so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Using usual screening conventions, estimate the 4p effective nuclear charge of bromine and of the bromide ion $Br^{-}$. Divide the neutral bromine value by the ion value and round the ratio to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: Neutral Br 4p gives $35 - 27.40 = 7.60$ and $Br^{-}$ 4p gives $35 - 27.75 = 7.25$. The ratio $7.60/7.25 = 1.05$ rounds to 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 4p electron of a krypton atom (Z = 36, $[Ar]3d^{10}4s^2 4p^6$), using the usual screening conventions. Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: The seven other 4s/4p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.45$. The eighteen 3s, 3p and 3d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$, and the ten inner electrons screen $1.00$ each for $10.00$. Total screening is $27.75$, so $Z_{eff} = 36 - 27.75 = 8.25$. Copying the bromide value gives 7.25, ignoring the 3d shielding gives 16.75, and reporting total screening gives 27.75.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the sizes and electron gain enthalpies of selected p-block ions and atoms. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: A) The ionic radius of $Br^{-}$ (196 pm) is larger than that of $Cl^{-}$ (181 pm).
B) The ionic radius of $Sr^{2+}$ (118 pm) is smaller than that of $Rb^{+}$ (152 pm).
C) The ionic radius of $Se^{2-}$ (198 pm) is smaller than that of $Te^{2-}$ (221 pm).
D) The ionic radius of $Br^{-}$ (196 pm) is larger than that of $Se^{2-}$ (198 pm).
questions.explanation: Going down a group increases ionic size, and $Br^{-}$ (196) exceeds $Cl^{-}$ (181), so A is correct. $Sr^{2+}$ (118) is smaller than $Rb^{+}$ (152), so B is correct. $Se^{2-}$ (198) is smaller than $Te^{2-}$ (221), so C is correct. $Br^{-}$ (196) is smaller than $Se^{2-}$ (198) because the two extra electrons on $Se^{2-}$ enlarge its cloud, so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Count how many of the following statements about krypton and xenon are correct. (i) The first ionisation enthalpy of Ar is higher than that of Kr. (ii) The first ionisation enthalpy of Kr is higher than that of Xe. (iii) The first ionisation enthalpy of Ne is lower than that of He. (iv) The 4p effective nuclear charge of Br is higher than that of Kr.
questions.explanation: Ar $(1521)$ is above Kr $(1351)$ kJ/mol, so (i) is correct. Kr $(1351)$ is above Xe $(1170)$, so (ii) is correct. He $(2372)$ is higher than Ne $(2081)$, so (iii) is false. The Kr 4p value of $Z_{eff} = 8.25$ exceeds the Br 4p value of $7.60$, so (iv) is false. Two statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge experienced by one 5p electron of a neutral tin atom (Z = 50, $[Kr]4d^{10}5s^2 5p^2$), using the usual screening conventions. Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: The three other 5s/5p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.05$. The eighteen 4s, 4p and 4d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$. The twenty-eight electrons in the 1s to 3d shells screen $1.00$ each for $28.00$. Total screening is $44.35$, so $Z_{eff} = 50 - 44.35 = 5.65$. Copying a 6.35 value from a lighter element is a common slip, treating the 4d electrons as fully shielding gives 4.15, and reporting total screening gives 44.35.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge experienced by one 5p electron of a neutral tellurium atom (Z = 52, $[Kr]4d^{10}5s^2 5p^4$), using the usual screening conventions. Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: The five other 5s/5p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.75$. The eighteen 4s, 4p and 4d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$. The twenty-eight electrons in the 1s to 3d shells screen $1.00$ each for $28.00$. Total screening is $45.05$, so $Z_{eff} = 52 - 45.05 = 6.95$. Copying the bromine 4p value gives 7.60, ignoring the 4d shielding gives 15.45, and reporting total screening gives 45.05.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Divide the 5p effective nuclear charge of neutral tellurium by that of neutral tin, both estimated with usual screening conventions, and round the ratio to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: Tellurium 5p gives $52 - 45.05 = 6.95$ and tin 5p gives $50 - 44.35 = 5.65$. The ratio $6.95/5.65 = 1.23$ rounds to 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 4p electron of the selenide ion $Se^{2-}$ (Z = 34, 36 electrons, $[Kr]$), using the usual screening conventions. Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: The seven other 4s/4p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.45$. The eighteen 3s, 3p and 3d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$, and the ten inner electrons screen $10.00$. Total screening is $27.75$, so $Z_{eff} = 34 - 27.75 = 6.25$. The neutral selenium value is 6.95, the bromide value is 7.25, and 27.75 is the total screening.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Count how many of these effective nuclear charges exceed 6.00: the 4p value of $Se^{2-}$, the 4p value of $Br^{-}$, the 5p value of neutral Te, the 5p value of neutral Sn, and the 3d value of neutral Ga (Z = 31).
questions.explanation: The values are $Se^{2-}$ 6.25, $Br^{-}$ 7.25, Te 5p 6.95, Sn 5p 5.65 and Ga 3d 9.85. Four of them (all except Sn 5p) exceed 6.00, so the count is 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the percentage ionic character of the Te-I bond using Pauling electronegativities of 2.10 for Te and 2.66 for I, rounded to the nearest whole percent.
questions.explanation: The difference is $\Delta\chi = 0.56$, so $\Delta\chi^2/4 = 0.3136/4 = 0.0784$. The ionic character is $100(1 - e^{-0.0784}) = 100(1 - 0.9246) = 7.54$, which rounds to 8. Quoting the covalent fraction gives 92, reporting the raw difference gives 56, and rounding the value down gives 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Arrange the 4p effective nuclear charges of As (Z = 33), Se (Z = 34), Br (Z = 35) and Kr (Z = 36) from lowest to highest, using usual screening conventions. Which ordering is correct?
questions.explanation: The computed 4p values are $6.30$ (As), $6.95$ (Se), $7.60$ (Br) and $8.25$ (Kr), which increase steadily across the period. Option B places Se below As, option C places Br below Se, and option D places Kr below Br.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charges of selected valence and inner electrons of germanium (Z = 32, $[Ar]3d^{10}4s^2 4p^2$) and nearby atoms, using usual screening conventions. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: A) The 4s electrons of Ge feel about the same effective nuclear charge as its 4p electrons.
B) The 4s electrons of Ge feel a higher effective nuclear charge than the 4s electrons of Ga.
C) The 4s electrons of Zn feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of Ge.
D) The 4s electrons of Ge feel a higher effective nuclear charge than its 3d electrons.
questions.explanation: Ge 4s gives $Z_{eff} = 32 - 26.35 = 5.65$, the same as Ge 4p, so A is correct. Ga 4s gives $31 - 26.00 = 5.00$, below Ge's 5.65, so B is correct. Zn 4s gives $30 - 25.65 = 4.35$, which is lower than Ge's value, so C is false. Ge 3d gives $32 - 21.15 = 10.85$, far above the 4s value, so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A $1.58$ g sample of pure $KMnO_4$ (molar mass $158$ g mol$^{-1}$) is dissolved, acidified with dilute sulphuric acid and added to an excess of $Fe^{2+}$ solution until all the permanganate has reacted. How many millimoles of $Fe^{2+}$ are oxidised to $Fe^{3+}$?
questions.explanation: Moles of permanganate are $1.58/158 = 0.0100$ mol. In acid each $MnO_4^-$ gains 5 electrons ($Mn^{7+} \to Mn^{2+}$), so the electrons gained are $5 \times 0.0100 = 0.0500$ mol. Each $Fe^{2+}$ loses one electron, so $0.0500$ mol $Fe^{2+}$ is oxidised, which is 50 millimoles.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A $25$ mL aliquot of $0.02$ M acidified $KMnO_4$ is titrated against $0.05$ M oxalic acid, $H_2C_2O_4$, until the permanganate is just consumed. What volume of the oxalic acid solution, in mL, is required?
questions.explanation: Permanganate present is $0.02 \times 25 = 0.500$ mmol, and it gains $5 \times 0.500 = 2.50$ mmol electrons. Each oxalic acid molecule gives 2 electrons (two carbons go from $+3$ to $+4$), so $1.25$ mmol $H_2C_2O_4$ is needed. Volume $= 1.25/0.05 = 25$ mL.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Potassium dichromate, $K_2Cr_2O_7$ (molar mass $294$ g mol$^{-1}$), is reduced to $Cr^{3+}$ in acidic medium. What is the equivalent mass of $K_2Cr_2O_7$ in this reduction?
questions.explanation: Each $Cr$ changes from $+6$ to $+3$, gaining 3 electrons, and the formula unit has two $Cr$ atoms, so 6 electrons are gained per formula unit. Equivalent mass $= 294/6 = 49$ g eq$^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The unbalanced equation $MnO_4^- + C_2O_4^{2-} \to Mn^{2+} + CO_2$ is balanced in acidic medium with smallest whole-number coefficients. Which option gives the coefficient of $H^+$ on the reactant side and of $H_2O$ on the product side?
questions.explanation: Electron balance needs $2MnO_4^-$ (gaining 10 e) with $5C_2O_4^{2-}$ (losing 10 e). Charge and oxygen balance then give $2MnO_4^- + 5C_2O_4^{2-} + 16H^+ \to 2Mn^{2+} + 10CO_2 + 8H_2O$, so $H^+ = 16$ and $H_2O = 8$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Chlorine gas is passed into hot concentrated sodium hydroxide solution until $1.8$ mol of $Cl_2$ has reacted, giving only chloride and chlorate ions. How many moles of electrons are transferred in total?
questions.explanation: The balanced equation is $3Cl_2 + 6OH^- \to 5Cl^- + ClO_3^- + 3H_2O$. Five chlorine atoms each gain one electron (5 electrons), while one chlorine atom loses 5 electrons to form $ClO_3^-$. Per 3 mol $Cl_2$, 5 mol electrons move, so $1.8 \times 5/3 = 3.0$ mol electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Sodium thiosulphate, $Na_2S_2O_3$ (molar mass $158$ g mol$^{-1}$), reacts with iodine and is converted to tetrathionate, $S_4O_6^{2-}$. What is the equivalent mass of $Na_2S_2O_3$ in this change?
questions.explanation: In $S_2O_3^{2-}$ the two sulphur atoms have average oxidation state $+2$; in $S_4O_6^{2-}$ the average is $+2.5$. Each $S_2O_3^{2-}$ therefore loses $2 \times 0.5 = 1$ electron. Equivalent mass $= 158/1 = 158$ g eq$^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A copper salt solution contains $1.5$ mmol of $Cu^{2+}$. Excess $KI$ is added, forming $CuI$ and iodine, and the liberated iodine is titrated with $0.1$ M $Na_2S_2O_3$. What volume of the thiosulphate solution, in mL, is required?
questions.explanation: Two $Cu^{2+}$ ions give one $I_2$ ($2Cu^{2+} + 4I^- \to 2CuI + I_2$), so $1.5$ mmol $Cu^{2+}$ gives $0.75$ mmol $I_2$. Each $I_2$ consumes two thiosulphate ions, needing $1.5$ mmol $S_2O_3^{2-}$. Volume $= 1.5/0.1 = 15$ mL.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Potassium dichromate oxidises hydrogen sulphide in acidic solution to sulphur. In the balanced equation with smallest integer coefficients, how many moles of $H_2S$ are oxidised per mole of $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$?
questions.explanation: Each $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ accepts 6 electrons ($2 \times 3$). Each $H_2S$ gives 2 electrons when $S^{2-}$ becomes $S$, so $6/2 = 3$ mol $H_2S$ are oxidised per mole of dichromate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Hydrogen peroxide is reduced to water in acidic solution. What is the equivalent mass of $H_2O_2$ (molar mass $34$ g mol$^{-1}$) in this reaction?
questions.explanation: Each oxygen atom in $H_2O_2$ changes from $-1$ to $-2$, so each $H_2O_2$ gains 2 electrons. Equivalent mass $= 34/2 = 17$ g eq$^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Nitrate ions are reduced to ammonia in strongly acidic solution. How many millimoles of electrons are needed to convert $4.0$ mmol of $NO_3^-$ completely into $NH_3$?
questions.explanation: In $NO_3^-$ nitrogen is $+5$, and in $NH_3$ it is $-3$. Each nitrogen gains 8 electrons, so $4.0$ mmol of nitrate needs $4.0 \times 8 = 32$ mmol of electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Acidified $H_2O_2$ reacts with $KMnO_4$, and oxygen is evolved. A sample of $5.1$ g $H_2O_2$ (molar mass $34$ g mol$^{-1}$) is completely consumed in this reaction. How many millimoles of $KMnO_4$ are needed?
questions.explanation: Moles of $H_2O_2$ are $5.1/34 = 0.150$ mol. The balanced reaction is $2MnO_4^- + 5H_2O_2 + 6H^+ \to 2Mn^{2+} + 5O_2 + 8H_2O$, so $0.150 \times 2/5 = 0.060$ mol of $KMnO_4$, which is 60 millimoles.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In basic medium, $MnO_4^-$ oxidises $SO_3^{2-}$ to $SO_4^{2-}$ and is itself reduced to $MnO_2$. When the equation is balanced with smallest whole-number coefficients, what is the coefficient of $OH^-$ on the product side?
questions.explanation: Each $MnO_4^-$ gains 3 electrons and each $SO_3^{2-}$ loses 2. The balanced equation is $2MnO_4^- + 3SO_3^{2-} + H_2O \to 2MnO_2 + 3SO_4^{2-} + 2OH^-$, so the product-side $OH^-$ coefficient is 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A $75$ mL solution of $0.02$ M potassium dichromate is added to an acidic solution of $Fe^{2+}$ until the dichromate is fully reduced to $Cr^{3+}$. How many millimoles of $Fe^{2+}$ are oxidised?
questions.explanation: Dichromate taken is $0.02 \times 75 = 1.50$ mmol. Each $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ accepts 6 electrons and each $Fe^{2+}$ gives one, so $6 \times 1.50 = 9.0$ mmol $Fe^{2+}$ is oxidised.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Chromium(III) oxide is fused with potassium chlorate and KOH to form potassium chromate, with the chlorate reduced to chloride. Which statement correctly gives the mole ratio of $KClO_3$ to $Cr_2O_3$ required, and the reason?
options: A) $1$ mol $KClO_3$ per mol $Cr_2O_3$, because the 6 electrons lost by the two $Cr^{3+}$ ions are gained by one $ClO_3^-$
B) $3$ mol $KClO_3$ per mol $Cr_2O_3$, because each $Cr^{3+}$ loses 3 electrons and the chlorate gains 1
C) $2$ mol $KClO_3$ per mol $Cr_2O_3$, because each $Cr^{3+}$ loses 1 electron
D) $6$ mol $KClO_3$ per mol $Cr_2O_3$, because each chlorate gains 1 electron
questions.explanation: Each $Cr^{3+}$ goes to $CrO_4^{2-}$ (chromium from $+3$ to $+6$), losing 3 electrons, so the two chromium atoms in $Cr_2O_3$ lose 6 electrons. Chlorate changes from $Cl^{+5}$ to $Cl^{-1}$, gaining 6 electrons per $ClO_3^-$, so the ratio is 1:1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Acidified permanganate oxidises hydrogen sulphide to sulphur. If $1.2$ mol of $MnO_4^-$ reacts completely with excess $H_2S$ in acid, how many moles of sulphur are formed?
questions.explanation: The balanced equation $2MnO_4^- + 5H_2S + 6H^+ \to 2Mn^{2+} + 5S + 8H_2O$ gives 5 mol S per 2 mol $MnO_4^-$. Thus $1.2 \times 5/2 = 3.0$ mol of sulphur are formed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For $MnO_4^- + Fe^{2+} \to Mn^{2+} + Fe^{3+}$ in acidic medium, consider these statements after balancing with smallest integers: (i) 1 mol $MnO_4^-$ oxidises 5 mol $Fe^{2+}$. (ii) $H_2O$ appears on the product side with coefficient 8. (iii) $H^+$ appears on the reactant side with coefficient 8. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: The balanced equation is $MnO_4^- + 5Fe^{2+} + 8H^+ \to Mn^{2+} + 5Fe^{3+} + 4H_2O$. Statement (i) holds, statement (iii) holds with 8 $H^+$, and statement (ii) is false because water has coefficient 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A $0.49$ g sample of pure potassium dichromate, $K_2Cr_2O_7$ (molar mass $294$ g mol$^{-1}$), is used to oxidise $Sn^{2+}$ to $Sn^{4+}$ completely. How many millimoles of $Sn^{2+}$ are oxidised?
questions.explanation: Dichromate moles are $0.49/294 = 1.667$ mmol. Each dichromate gains 6 electrons, giving $10.0$ mmol of electrons. Each $Sn^{2+}$ loses 2 electrons, so $10.0/2 = 5$ mmol $Sn^{2+}$ is oxidised.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Given standard reduction potentials $E^{\circ}(Sn^{4+}/Sn^{2+}) = +0.15$ V and $E^{\circ}(Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}) = +0.77$ V, which option gives the standard cell potential for $Sn^{2+} + 2Fe^{3+} \to Sn^{4+} + 2Fe^{2+}$ and its spontaneity?
questions.explanation: The cell potential is $E^{\circ}_{cell} = E^{\circ}_{cathode} - E^{\circ}_{anode} = 0.77 - 0.15 = +0.62$ V. A positive value means the reaction is spontaneous.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A galvanic cell $Zn \mid Zn^{2+}$ (0.1 M) $\| Cu^{2+}$ (1.0 M) $\mid Cu$ operates at 298 K. Take $E^{\circ}(Zn^{2+}/Zn) = -0.76$ V and $E^{\circ}(Cu^{2+}/Cu) = +0.34$ V. The cell potential is closest to:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In acidic solution $H_2S$ is oxidised to sulphur by nitric acid, which is reduced to nitric oxide, NO. How many moles of $HNO_3$ are reduced when $9$ mol of $H_2S$ is completely oxidised to sulphur?
questions.explanation: The balanced equation is $3H_2S + 2HNO_3 \to 3S + 2NO + 4H_2O$. Each $H_2S$ gives 2 electrons and each $N$ gains 3, so 9 mol $H_2S$ supplies 18 electrons, which reduces $18/3 = 6$ mol $HNO_3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Chromium(III) hydroxide is oxidised by hypochlorite in strongly basic solution to chromate, while hypochlorite is reduced to chloride. Balanced with smallest whole-number coefficients, which option gives the coefficients of $OH^-$ (reactant side) and $H_2O$ (product side)?
questions.explanation: The balanced equation is $2Cr(OH)_3 + 3ClO^- + 4OH^- \to 2CrO_4^{2-} + 3Cl^- + 5H_2O$. Chromium loses 6 electrons in total and three hypochlorite ions gain 6, and hydrogen and oxygen balance then fix $OH^- = 4$ and $H_2O = 5$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For $2Cu^{2+} + 4I^- \to 2CuI + I_2$, consider: (i) each $Cu^{2+}$ gains one electron. (ii) Two mol $Cu^{2+}$ produce one mol $I_2$. (iii) $I^-$ is reduced to $I_2$. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Each $Cu^{2+}$ becomes $Cu^+$ in CuI and gains one electron, so 2 mol $Cu^{2+}$ gain 2 electrons, which two $I^-$ release as one $I_2$. Statement (iii) is false because $I^-$ is oxidised, not reduced.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Sulphur is heated with concentrated sodium hydroxide and disproportionates to sulphide and sulphite ions only. How many moles of $S^{2-}$ are formed from $4.5$ mol of sulphur atoms?
questions.explanation: The balanced equation is $3S + 6OH^- \to 2S^{2-} + SO_3^{2-} + 3H_2O$. Three sulphur atoms give two sulphide ions, so $4.5 \times 2/3 = 3.0$ mol $S^{2-}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In acidic medium iodate ion is reduced to iodine, $IO_3^- \to I_2$. Which option gives the equivalent mass of $KIO_3$ (molar mass $214$ g mol$^{-1}$) in this change, together with the correct reason?
options: A) $42.8$ g eq$^{-1}$, because each iodate ion gains 5 electrons
B) $107$ g eq$^{-1}$, because each iodate ion gains 2 electrons
C) $214$ g eq$^{-1}$, because iodate gains no electrons overall
D) $21.4$ g eq$^{-1}$, because each iodate ion gains 10 electrons
questions.explanation: Iodine goes from $+5$ in $IO_3^-$ to $0$ in $I_2$, so each iodate gains 5 electrons. Equivalent mass $= 214/5 = 42.8$ g eq$^{-1}$. Two iodate ions give one $I_2$ with 10 electrons, which is still 5 per ion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Hydrogen peroxide is used with acidified permanganate and with iodide ions. Consider: (i) $H_2O_2$ acts as a reducing agent towards acidic $KMnO_4$ and oxygen is released. (ii) $H_2O_2$ oxidises $I^-$ to $I_2$ in acid. (iii) $H_2O_2$ reduces $MnO_4^-$ to $MnO_2$ in acid. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: In acid, $2MnO_4^- + 5H_2O_2 + 6H^+ \to 2Mn^{2+} + 5O_2 + 8H_2O$, so (i) holds. The reaction $H_2O_2 + 2I^- + 2H^+ \to I_2 + 2H_2O$ shows (ii) is true. Statement (iii) is false because in acid manganese is reduced to $Mn^{2+}$, not $MnO_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Sulphur dioxide is passed into an acidified solution containing $4$ mol of dichromate ions, $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$, until all of it is reduced to $Cr^{3+}$. How many moles of $SO_2$ are oxidised to sulphate?
questions.explanation: The balanced equation is $Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 3SO_2 + 2H^+ \to 2Cr^{3+} + 3SO_4^{2-} + H_2O$. Each dichromate needs 3 $SO_2$ molecules, so $4 \times 3 = 12$ mol $SO_2$ are oxidised.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Tin(II) ions reduce nitrate ions in acidic solution to nitric oxide, and tin is oxidised to tin(IV). When $3Sn^{2+} + 2NO_3^- + xH^+ \to 3Sn^{4+} + 2NO + yH_2O$ is balanced with smallest integers, what are $x$ and $y$?
questions.explanation: Electron balance: the three $Sn^{2+}$ lose 6 electrons and the two $NO_3^-$ gain 6. Charge balance needs $-2 + x = +12$, so $x = 8$. Oxygen balance gives $6 = 2 + y$, so $y = 4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Starting with $9$ mol of $H_2S$ and $3$ mol of $SO_2$, the reaction between them goes to completion in solution. How many moles of elemental sulphur are formed?
questions.explanation: The balanced equation is $2H_2S + SO_2 \to 3S + 2H_2O$. Each $SO_2$ gives 3 sulphur atoms, so $3 \times 3 = 9$ mol of S. The $H_2S$ is in excess, since 3 mol $SO_2$ needs only 6 mol $H_2S$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Standard reduction potentials are $E^{\circ}(Ag^+/Ag) = +0.80$ V, $E^{\circ}(Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}) = +0.77$ V and $E^{\circ}(Cu^{2+}/Cu) = +0.34$ V. Which statements are correct? (i) Cu can reduce $Ag^+$ to Ag. (ii) $Fe^{2+}$ can reduce $Ag^+$ to Ag. (iii) Ag can reduce $Fe^{3+}$ to $Fe^{2+}$.
questions.explanation: For (i), $E^{\circ}_{cell} = 0.80 - 0.34 = +0.46$ V. For (ii), $0.80 - 0.77 = +0.03$ V. Both are positive, so both are spontaneous. For (iii), $0.77 - 0.80 = -0.03$ V, so it is non-spontaneous.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Copper metal is placed in a solution of silver ions, and the reaction $Cu + 2Ag^+ \to Cu^{2+} + 2Ag$ occurs with $E^{\circ}(Ag^+/Ag) = +0.80$ V and $E^{\circ}(Cu^{2+}/Cu) = +0.34$ V. Taking $F = 96485$ C mol$^{-1}$, what is the magnitude of $\Delta G^{\circ}$ in kJ mol$^{-1}$, rounded to the nearest integer?
questions.explanation: $E^{\circ}_{cell} = 0.80 - 0.34 = 0.46$ V and $n = 2$. Then $|\Delta G^{\circ}| = nFE^{\circ} = 2 \times 96485 \times 0.46 = 88766$ J, which is $88.8 \approx 89$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Cuprous ion disproportionates: $2Cu^+ \to Cu^{2+} + Cu$. Given $E^{\circ}(Cu^{2+}/Cu^+) = +0.15$ V and $E^{\circ}(Cu^+/Cu) = +0.52$ V, which option gives the standard cell potential for this process and its status?
questions.explanation: The reduction of $Cu^+$ to $Cu$ (+0.52 V) acts as the cathode, and the reduction of $Cu^{2+}$ to $Cu^+$ (+0.15 V) runs in reverse at the anode. So $E^{\circ}_{cell} = 0.52 - 0.15 = +0.37$ V, which is positive, so the process is spontaneous.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A sample of $11.6$ g of magnetite, $Fe_3O_4$ (molar mass $232$ g mol$^{-1}$), is treated with acidified $KMnO_4$ so that only its $Fe^{2+}$ is oxidised to $Fe^{3+}$. How many millimoles of $KMnO_4$ are required?
questions.explanation: Moles of $Fe_3O_4$ are $11.6/232 = 0.0500$ mol. Each formula unit has one $Fe^{2+}$, releasing one electron, so 50 mmol electrons are released. Permanganate gains 5 electrons per ion, so it needs $50/5 = 10$ mmol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Acidified potassium dichromate oxidises a mixture containing $0.6$ mol $Fe^{2+}$ and $0.3$ mol $SO_3^{2-}$ completely, with dichromate reduced to $Cr^{3+}$. Which option gives the moles of dichromate required, together with the reason?
options: A) $0.1$ mol, because $Fe^{2+}$ alone accounts for all the electrons
B) $0.2$ mol, because $Fe^{2+}$ needs $0.1$ mol and sulphite needs $0.1$ mol
C) $0.3$ mol, because each sulphite ion and each $Fe^{2+}$ ion give 2 electrons
D) $0.4$ mol, because each $Fe^{2+}$ and each sulphite ion uses 6 electrons
questions.explanation: Each dichromate accepts 6 electrons. $0.6$ mol $Fe^{2+}$ gives $0.6$ mol electrons, needing $0.1$ mol dichromate. $0.3$ mol $SO_3^{2-}$ gives $0.6$ mol electrons (sulphur $+4$ to $+6$), needing another $0.1$ mol. The total is $0.2$ mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In acidic solution permanganate oxidises nitrite ions to nitrate ions. How many moles of nitrite ions are oxidised by $3.2$ mol of permanganate?
questions.explanation: Each permanganate gains 5 electrons, and each nitrite loses 2 electrons as nitrogen goes from $+3$ to $+5$. The balanced equation $2MnO_4^- + 5NO_2^- + 6H^+ \to 2Mn^{2+} + 5NO_3^- + 3H_2O$ gives $3.2 \times 5/2 = 8.0$ mol $NO_2^-$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: $KMnO_4$ is used as an oxidant in two media. In strongly acidic solution it is reduced to $Mn^{2+}$, and in strongly alkaline solution it is reduced to $MnO_4^{2-}$. What is the ratio of the equivalent mass of $KMnO_4$ in alkaline medium to its equivalent mass in acidic medium?
questions.explanation: In acid, manganese changes from $+7$ to $+2$, a gain of 5 electrons. In alkali it changes to $+6$, a gain of 1 electron. Equivalent mass is molar mass divided by $n$, so the ratio is $(M/1)/(M/5) = 5$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider two acidic-medium reactions: P, in which dichromate $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ oxidises $H_2S$ to sulphur, and Q, in which chlorate $ClO_3^-$ oxidises $I^-$ to $I_2$ with $Cl^-$ formed. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: A) In P, 3 mol $H_2S$ are oxidised per mol $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$, and 7 mol $H_2O$ are formed.
B) In Q, 1 mol $ClO_3^-$ oxidises 6 mol $I^-$, forming 3 mol $I_2$.
C) In Q, 6 mol $H^+$ are consumed and 6 mol $H_2O$ are formed per mol $ClO_3^-$.
D) In P, each sulphur atom loses 2 electrons and each $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ gains 6 electrons.
questions.explanation: In P, $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ gains 6 electrons (two $Cr$ from $+6$ to $+3$), and 3 $H_2S$ supply 6 electrons, giving $Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 3H_2S + 8H^+ \to 2Cr^{3+} + 3S + 7H_2O$. In Q, $ClO_3^-$ gains 6 electrons ($+5$ to $-1$), giving $ClO_3^- + 6I^- + 6H^+ \to Cl^- + 3I_2 + 3H_2O$. Statement C is false because only 3 mol water forms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: At 298 K, $Cu + 2Ag^+ \to Cu^{2+} + 2Ag$ has $E^{\circ}(Ag^+/Ag) = +0.80$ V and $E^{\circ}(Cu^{2+}/Cu) = +0.34$ V. A solution has $[Cu^{2+}] = 0.001$ M and $[Ag^+] = 0.1$ M. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: A) The standard cell potential is $+0.46$ V.
B) Under these concentrations the cell potential is about $+0.49$ V.
C) Under these concentrations the forward reaction is non-spontaneous.
D) Raising $[Ag^+]$ to 1.0 M increases the cell potential above its value at 0.1 M.
questions.explanation: The standard value is $0.80 - 0.34 = 0.46$ V. The reaction quotient is $Q = [Cu^{2+}]/[Ag^+]^2 = 0.001/0.01 = 0.1$, so $E = 0.46 - \frac{0.0592}{2}\log(0.1) = 0.49$ V, which is positive and spontaneous. At $[Ag^+] = 1.0$ M, $Q = 0.001$ and $E = 0.46 + 0.089 = 0.55$ V, which is higher.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A mixture of $0.04$ mol $Fe^{2+}$ and $0.03$ mol oxalate ion, $C_2O_4^{2-}$, is completely oxidised by acidified $MnO_4^-$. Express the moles of $MnO_4^-$ consumed as an integer multiple of $0.01$ mol.
questions.explanation: The $Fe^{2+}$ supplies $0.04$ mol electrons. Each oxalate gives 2 electrons (two carbons from $+3$ to $+4$), so $0.03 \times 2 = 0.06$ mol electrons. The total is $0.10$ mol. Permanganate gains 5 electrons per ion, so $0.10/5 = 0.02$ mol $= 2 \times 0.01$ mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Manganate ions disproportionate in slightly acidic solution to permanganate and manganese dioxide. Starting with $1.2$ mol of $MnO_4^{2-}$, express the moles of $MnO_4^-$ formed as an integer multiple of $0.1$ mol.
questions.explanation: The balanced equation is $3MnO_4^{2-} + 4H^+ \to 2MnO_4^- + MnO_2 + 2H_2O$, so 2 mol $MnO_4^-$ form per 3 mol manganate. Thus $1.2 \times 2/3 = 0.8$ mol $= 8 \times 0.1$ mol. Electron balance: two Mn go from $+6$ to $+7$ (2 electrons lost) and one goes to $+4$ (2 electrons gained).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Using $E^{\circ}(Ag^+/Ag) = +0.80$ V and $E^{\circ}(Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}) = +0.77$ V at 298 K, the equilibrium constant for $Ag^+ + Fe^{2+} \rightleftharpoons Ag + Fe^{3+}$ is closest to:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Chlorine behaves differently in cold dilute and hot concentrated alkali. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: A) In cold dilute $NaOH$, $Cl_2 + 2OH^- \to Cl^- + ClO^- + H_2O$, so 1 mol $Cl_2$ gives 1 mol each of $Cl^-$ and $ClO^-$.
B) In hot concentrated $NaOH$, 3 mol $Cl_2$ give 5 mol $Cl^-$ and 1 mol $ClO_3^-$.
C) The change $3ClO^- \to ClO_3^- + 2Cl^-$ transfers 4 electrons for every 3 mol of $ClO^-$.
D) In cold dilute $NaOH$, 2 mol $Cl_2$ give 1 mol $ClO_3^-$ as the main product.
questions.explanation: In cold dilute alkali, $Cl_2$ disproportionates 1:1 to $Cl^-$ and $ClO^-$. In hot alkali, $3Cl_2 + 6OH^- \to 5Cl^- + ClO_3^- + 3H_2O$. For statement C, one chlorine goes from $+1$ to $+5$ (4 electrons lost) and two go from $+1$ to $-1$ (2 electrons each, 4 total). Statement D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the basic-medium reaction $2Bi(OH)_3 + 3SnO_2^{2-} \to 2Bi + 3SnO_3^{2-} + 3H_2O$, which statement correctly describes the electron transfer?
options: A) Each $Bi(OH)_3$ gains 3 electrons, and each $SnO_2^{2-}$ loses 2 electrons.
B) Each $Bi(OH)_3$ gains 3 electrons, and each $SnO_2^{2-}$ also gains 2 electrons.
C) Each $Bi(OH)_3$ loses 3 electrons, and each $SnO_2^{2-}$ gains 2 electrons.
D) Each $Bi(OH)_3$ gains 2 electrons, and each $SnO_2^{2-}$ loses 3 electrons.
questions.explanation: Bismuth goes from $+3$ to $0$, so each $Bi(OH)_3$ gains 3 electrons. Tin goes from $+2$ in $SnO_2^{2-}$ to $+4$ in $SnO_3^{2-}$, losing 2 electrons per ion. Six electrons are gained by two Bi and six are lost by three Sn, which balances.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A solution contains $0.06$ mol $Sn^{2+}$ and $0.06$ mol $Fe^{2+}$. Acidified potassium dichromate is added until both are fully oxidised. Express the moles of dichromate consumed as an integer multiple of $0.01$ mol.
questions.explanation: $Sn^{2+}$ gives $0.12$ mol electrons (2 each) and $Fe^{2+}$ gives $0.06$ mol (1 each), a total of $0.18$ mol. Each dichromate accepts 6 electrons, so $0.18/6 = 0.03$ mol $= 3 \times 0.01$ mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: White phosphorus is heated in alkali and disproportionates to phosphine and hypophosphite ions only. Express the moles of $H_2PO_2^-$ formed from $0.3$ mol of $P_4$ as an integer multiple of $0.1$ mol.
questions.explanation: Each $P_4$ gives 3 mol $H_2PO_2^-$, so $0.3 \times 3 = 0.9$ mol $= 9 \times 0.1$ mol. Electron balance: three P atoms go from $0$ to $+1$ (3 electrons lost) while one goes from $0$ to $-3$ (3 electrons gained).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: At 298 K the half reaction $MnO_4^- + 8H^+ + 5e^- \to Mn^{2+} + 4H_2O$ has $E^{\circ} = +1.51$ V. In a solution with $[MnO_4^-] = 0.1$ M, $[Mn^{2+}] = 0.01$ M and $[H^+] = 0.1$ M, the electrode potential is closest to:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Given standard reduction potentials $E^{\circ}(Au^{3+}/Au) = +1.50$ V, $E^{\circ}(Cl_2/Cl^-) = +1.36$ V, $E^{\circ}(Ag^+/Ag) = +0.80$ V and $E^{\circ}(Pb^{2+}/Pb) = -0.13$ V, which of the following statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: For A, $E^{\circ}_{cell} = 1.36 - (-0.13) = 1.49$ V, which is positive. For B, $1.50 - 0.80 = 0.70$ V. For C, $0.80 - (-0.13) = 0.93$ V. For D, $-0.13 - 0.80 = -0.93$ V, so it is not spontaneous.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In acidic solution $H_2O_2$ reduces $MnO_4^-$ to $Mn^{2+}$ and is itself oxidised to oxygen gas. A $25$ mL aliquot of $0.04$ M $KMnO_4$ is titrated with $0.5$ M $H_2O_2$ until the permanganate is just consumed. What volume of $H_2O_2$ solution, in mL, is required?
questions.explanation: $25 \times 0.04 = 1.0$ mmol $MnO_4^-$ gains 5 electrons per ion, giving $5.0$ mmol electrons. Each $H_2O_2$ loses 2 electrons, so $2.5$ mmol $H_2O_2$ is needed. Volume $= 2.5/0.5 = 5$ mL.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Hydrogen peroxide reduces acidified dichromate, $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$, to $Cr^{3+}$ and is itself oxidised to oxygen gas. Express the moles of $O_2$ formed from $0.2$ mol of dichromate as an integer multiple of $0.1$ mol.
questions.explanation: The balanced equation is $Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 3H_2O_2 + 8H^+ \to 2Cr^{3+} + 3O_2 + 7H_2O$, so each dichromate gives 3 $O_2$ and $0.2 \times 3 = 0.6$ mol $= 6 \times 0.1$ mol. Dichromate gains 6 electrons while three $H_2O_2$ release 6 electrons as 3 $O_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A solution is prepared by dissolving $18$ g of glucose ($C_6H_{12}O_6$, molar mass $180$ g mol$^{-1}$) in $90$ g of water (molar mass $18$ g mol$^{-1}$). What is the mole fraction of water in this solution?
questions.explanation: Moles of glucose are $18/180 = 0.10$ mol and moles of water are $90/18 = 5.00$ mol, so the water mole fraction is $5.00/5.10 = 0.980$. Dividing the masses instead gives $90/108 = 0.833$, which mixes grams with moles. Converting $18$ g with $100$ instead of $180$ gives $0.965$, and reporting the glucose fraction $0.10/5.10$ gives $0.020$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A solution contains $10$ g of ethanol ($C_2H_5OH$, molar mass $46$ g mol$^{-1}$) dissolved in $90$ g of water, so the total mass is $100$ g. Find the molality of ethanol in mol kg$^{-1}$ of water, multiply that value by $10$, and round to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: Ethanol moles are $10/46 = 0.2174$ mol. The solvent mass is $90$ g $= 0.090$ kg, so the molality is $0.2174/0.090 = 2.415$ mol kg$^{-1}$. Multiplying by $10$ gives $24.15$, which rounds to $24$. Using the total $100$ g as solvent mass gives $2.174$ mol kg$^{-1}$ and an answer of $22$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: At a fixed temperature the vapour pressure of pure water is $31.8$ torr. A non-volatile solute of molar mass $60$ g mol$^{-1}$ is dissolved so that $30$ g of solute is present in $180$ g of water (molar mass $18$ g mol$^{-1}$). What is the vapour pressure of this solution?
questions.explanation: Solute moles are $30/60 = 0.50$ mol and water moles are $180/18 = 10.0$ mol, so the water mole fraction is $10.0/10.5 = 0.952$. Then $P = 31.8 \times 0.952 = 30.29$ torr. Using the mass ratio $180/210$ gives $27.26$ torr, treating the $30$ g of solute as $30$ mol gives $7.95$ torr, and using the solute mole fraction $0.0476$ instead gives $1.51$ torr.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A solution of a non-volatile solute in water raises the boiling point by $0.52$ K, where water has $K_b = 0.52$ K kg mol$^{-1}$.
